s: POSIX-shared network filesystem many instances mount concurrently - lift-and-shift compatibility layer.
w: Exported NFS-style trees scale capacity elastically; throughput modes (bursting/provisioned) shape performance. Locking semantics support concurrent writers imperfectly at scale; metadata operations (many small files) often bottleneck before byte throughput does.
use: Legacy apps expecting mounted directories (config shares, home dirs)
ML training scratch shared across GPU nodes
Content processing pipelines passing files between stages
WordPress/media farms with many web servers reading same tree
avoid: Massive unstructured archives with HTTP access (object_storage cheaper)
Millions-of-files metadata churn (object stores list faster)
pits: Metadata storms on huge dirs - shard directory trees
NFS locking quirks break some apps - test concurrency
tips: Distinguish cleanly: block=disks, file=shared folders, object=HTTP blobs
